tools.name: list_layers
tools.title: List layers
tools.description: List the layers of the open QGIS project that FilterMate knows, as {"layers": [...]}. Each layer has layer_id, name, provider_type, feature_count (-1 when unknown), geometry_type, crs_authid, layer_kind (vector, raster or point_cloud), has_active_filter and active_filter_expression (cut past 200 characters, with active_filter_expression_length: describe_layer gives it whole), visible (checked in the layer tree, with its groups) and group (the groups above it, joined by " / "). The layers come in the order of the layer tree, the one drawn on top first. "more" says how many matching layers were left out by limit. Call this first: the other tools take layer names or ids from it.

kind.description: Only the layers of this kind

name_contains.description: Only the layers whose name holds this text (case ignored)

tools.name: filter_status
tools.title: Filter status
tools.description: Snapshot of the filter session: status, active_filters ({layer name: subset string}), their count, last_applied_at / last_applied_layer / last_applied_source and last_error. Vector subset strings only. filter_state also covers raster and point cloud layers.

tools.name: filter_state
tools.title: Filter state
tools.description: Every layer FilterMate filters right now, of any kind, as {"layers": [...]}. Each row has layer_id, name, layer_kind, subset (the filter string, empty for a clipped raster; cut past 200 characters, with subset_length: describe_layer gives it whole) and derived (true when the layer reads a clipped copy of its source). Use it to check what a filter did, and to find out what a previous call did when a request timed out.

tools.name: list_favorites
tools.title: List favorites
tools.description: List the favorites (saved filters) of the FilterMate project, as {"favorites": [...]}. Each has favorite_id (what apply_favorite takes), name, description, layer_name and expression.

tools.name: describe_layer
tools.title: Describe a layer
tools.description: What a layer is and what a filter can test on it: its fields, bands or point attributes. Returns layer_id, name, layer_kind, provider_type, crs_authid, geometry_type, feature_count, subset (its current filter), visible and group (its place in the layer tree), extent ([xmin, ymin, xmax, ymax] in its own CRS, empty for a web service), style (how it is drawn: renderer, and when they apply field, classes (how many), labels (the field labelled), opacity, min_scale and max_scale (it only shows between these scale denominators)), and by kind: joins [{layer, field, target_field, prefix}] and relations [{name, role (parent or child), layer, fields}] for a vector layer, with sql_dialect (postgresql, sqlite, ogr_sql or qgis_expression: the language of its filter) and fields [{name, type, alias, filterable}] for a vector layer (filterable is false for virtual and joined fields, which a filter expression cannot test); bands [{band, name, classes}] and pixel_size for a raster, classes [{value, label}] only on a paletted band; attributes [name] for a point cloud.

layer.description: Layer id or name, of any kind

tools.name: field_values
tools.title: Values of a field
tools.description: Distinct values a field really takes, among the features the layer shows now (its filter applies). Use it to write a filter with the exact spelling of a value. Returns values, truncated (more values exist), and minimum and maximum for a numeric or date field. NULL is left out. Refused on web services (WFS...), which would have to be read whole.

search.description: Text fields: only values containing this text, ignoring case

tools.name: layer_statistics
tools.title: Statistics of a layer
tools.description: Count, sum, mean, minimum, maximum of a field or of the geometries of a vector layer, in all or by group. Computed on the features the layer shows now (its filter applies), or on its selection: use it to answer "how many", "what total", "which is the largest", and to check what a filter kept. With neither field nor measure it counts features, by group when group_by is given. Returns feature_count (features read), statistics {count, nulls, minimum, maximum, and sum, mean, stdev for numbers or distinct for text}, unit (m or m2 for a measure), and with group_by: groups [{value, feature_count, and the same statistics}], groups_total and truncated. Refused on web services and above 500000 features: filter or select first.

field.description: Field to sum up, from describe_layer. Leave empty to count features, or to use measure

group_by.description: Field whose values make the groups: one row of statistics per value

measure.description: Measure the geometries instead of a field: length of lines (perimeter of polygons) in metres, or area of polygons in square metres

limit.description: At most this many groups, the largest first

tools.name: sample_features
tools.title: Sample of features
tools.description: A few features of a vector layer with their attributes, to see what its rows look like. Among the features the layer shows now (its filter applies). Returns crs_authid, features [{fid, attributes {field: value}, geometry {type, centroid, bbox}}], truncated (more features match) and fields_truncated. Long text is cut at 200 characters. Refused on web services.

fields.description: Only these fields; the first 50 fields by default

expression.description: QGIS expression (NOT SQL) the features must match, as for select_features: "population" > 10000

geometry.description: Also the type, centroid and bounding box of each geometry, in the layer CRS

tools.name: identify_at
tools.title: Identify at a point
tools.description: What lies at a point of the map: the features of the vector layers and the values of the rasters there. As the Identify tool of QGIS. Returns layers, only those with something at the point: [{layer_name, layer_kind, features [{fid, attributes}], truncated}] for a vector layer, [{layer_name, layer_kind, values [{band, value}]}] for a raster; and skipped (web services, which are not read).

x.description: X or longitude of the point

y.description: Y or latitude of the point

crs.description: CRS of the point, such as EPSG:4326; the CRS of the map (canvas_crs of map_context) by default

layers.description: Only these layers (ids or names); the visible layers by default

tolerance.description: Search distance around the point, in the units of crs; five pixels of the map by default

limit.description: At most this many features per layer

tools.name: find_algorithms
tools.title: Find a Processing algorithm
tools.description: Find the Processing algorithms of QGIS the agent may run, by words of their id, name, group or tags. Only the algorithms of QGIS itself that make layers, or answer statistics, are listed: none that runs SQL or code, writes to a data source or a file, or reaches the network. Returns algorithms [{id, name, group, summary}] and total. Then describe_algorithm gives the parameters of one.

query.description: Words in English, as QGIS names its algorithms: buffer, centroids, dissolve, clip, join attributes, voronoi, heatmap, slope...

tools.name: describe_algorithm
tools.title: Describe a Processing algorithm
tools.description: What a Processing algorithm does, and how to give each of its parameters to run_algorithm. Returns help, parameters [{name, type, description, optional, default, options (an enum: give the index or the text), parent (the layer a field or a distance belongs to), minimum, maximum, value (how to give it), destination (an output: FilterMate writes it to a temporary layer)}] and outputs. left_out names parameters that cannot be given (files, folders, connections).

algorithm_id.description: Id from find_algorithms, such as native:buffer

tools.name: run_algorithm
tools.title: Run a Processing algorithm
tools.description: Run a Processing algorithm of QGIS on layers of the project; the layers it makes are added to the project. Each output layer is a temporary file: export_layers keeps one for good. In the chat of FilterMate, undoing the turn removes them. Returns layers [{output, layer_id, name, layer_kind, feature_count}], values (what the algorithm answers besides layers: statistics...), not_made and messages (its warnings). Inputs are layers of the project only, never a path or a URL; expressions take the functions of select_features and math, text and geometry ones.

parameters.description: Values by parameter name, as describe_algorithm says: layers by name or id, {"layer": ..., "selected_only": true} for the selected features of a source, numbers, text, the index or the text of an option. Outputs are written by FilterMate: leave them out, or pass false to skip an optional one.

names.description: Name of the layer made by each output, by output name (OUTPUT...)

tools.name: preview_filter
tools.title: Try a filter
tools.description: Try a filter expression on a private copy of the layer: nothing changes in the project. It is what apply_filter would do, and it replaces the layer's current filter in the same way. Returns valid, feature_count (features kept, -1 when unknown) and error (the reason when valid is false). Refused on web services and memory layers, and for anything but a plain condition (subqueries, most functions).

tools.name: map_context
tools.title: Map context
tools.description: What the user is looking at in QGIS. Returns project_crs, canvas_crs, extent_wkt (the visible extent, usable as is with geometry_filter and canvas_crs), extent (the same as [xmin, ymin, xmax, ymax]), scale, layouts (the print layouts of the project, by name), active_layer_id, active_layer_name, selections [{layer_id, name, selected_count}] (the layers with selected features, which cross_filter uses as its source) and drawn_objects [{layer_id, name, crs_authid, count, area_m2, extent_wkt}] (the rasters on which the user drew objects in the FilterMate dock: cross_filter uses them with that raster as source_layer and raster_selection {"dock_objects": true}). available is false when QGIS has no map canvas.

tools.name: apply_filter
tools.title: Apply a filter expression
tools.description: Set the filter (subset string) of one vector layer; without operator it replaces the previous filter. Returns success, expression (as applied), replaced_filter (the filter the layer had and lost, when no operator was given) and active_filters ({layer name: subset string} after the call). For spatial filtering between layers use cross_filter or geometry_filter. Revert with clear_filters. Caution: some providers (GeoPackage, Shapefile through OGR) accept an invalid SQL expression without any error and the layer then shows no feature. Check list_layers afterwards (feature_count -1, or 0 when you expected matches) and use clear_filters to recover.

layer_name.description: A VECTOR layer: its id, or its name (an id first; by name, the first vector layer of that name)

expression.description: Subset string: the provider's SQL WHERE clause, without the WHERE keyword. For a PostgreSQL, GeoPackage, Shapefile or Spatialite layer: "population" > 10000 AND "dep" = '31'. Quote field names with double quotes and text values with single quotes. Plain conditions only: comparisons, IN, LIKE, BETWEEN, IS NULL and simple text or number functions; a subquery or another function is refused.

source.description: Free-text tag shown in the FilterMate log to tell where the filter came from

operator.description: Combine with the layer's current filter instead of replacing it: AND narrows it (the new condition only, never a copy of the current filter), OR widens it, AND NOT removes the new condition from it

tools.name: undo_filter
tools.title: Undo the last vector filter
tools.description: Undo the last step of the dock's vector filter history (the dock's Undo button). Returns the step rolled back to (layer_name, expression, is_clear) and active_filters. Only steps recorded by the dock itself are undone: nothing done through these tools (apply_filter, cross_filter, geometry_filter, point_cloud_filter, clear_filters, apply_favorite) is, so use clear_filters to revert those. Fails with 'Nothing to undo' when the history is empty. Not idempotent: each call undoes one more step, so after an error or a timeout read filter_state before calling again.

tools.name: redo_filter
tools.title: Redo the last undone vector filter
tools.description: Redo the step undone last in the dock's vector filter history (the dock's Redo button). Same answer and same caution as undo_filter (not idempotent: read filter_state after an error or a timeout). Fails with 'Nothing to redo' when there is nothing to redo.

tools.name: cross_filter
tools.title: Cross filter
tools.description: Filter layers by their spatial relation to a selection made on a source layer, any kind to any kind. Source kinds: a vector layer (its selected features), a raster (pixels kept by raster_selection, e.g. elevation between 1200 and 1300) or a point cloud (points kept by point_cloud_criteria, e.g. class 6). Targets keep what satisfies the predicates: vector features, raster pixels or LiDAR points inside the source area (outside with Disjoint). Filters apply in place to the project layers and replace the previous filter of each target unless operator is given. Not recorded in the undo history: revert with clear_filters. Returns filtered (names of the layers filtered), failed ({layer: reason}), skipped ({layer: reason}) and warnings ({layer: reason}: filtered, but a web service read up to its budget, so features may be missing). A layer that is not found is reported in failed; a source that is not found is an error.

source_layer.description: Source layer, vector, raster or point cloud: layer id or name

target_layers.description: Layers to filter, of any kind: layer ids or names. The source itself is not filtered (except with filter_source).

predicates.description: Spatial predicates, each tested as `target <predicate> source`: Intersect (share any space), Contain (the target contains the source), Disjoint (share nothing; rasters and point clouds then keep the outside of the source), Equal (same geometry), Touch (borders meet, interiors do not), Overlap (partial overlap of same-dimension geometries), Are within (the target lies inside the source), Cross (lines crossing). A target is kept when ANY listed predicate holds.

buffer.description: Buffer applied to the source geometry before testing, in the source CRS units (metres for a projected CRS; for a geographic CRS the API treats them as metres). Negative shrinks. 0 = none.

coverage_min.description: Polygon targets only: minimum share (%) of the target that must lie inside the source

operator.description: How to combine with the previous filter of each target: AND (keep what both filters keep), OR (keep what either keeps), AND NOT (remove the new selection from the previous filter, or from the whole layer when it has none). Omit to replace the previous filter.

selected_only.description: Vector source: use the features currently selected in QGIS; with none selected, the features its filter keeps. A web service source such as WFS must be selected or already filtered, it is never read whole. select_features changes the selection; false uses all the features the source shows.

anyOf.description: Pixels kept on a raster source (same rules as the EXPLORING raster panel of the dock).

mode.description: range: pixels between minimum and maximum; classes: pixels whose value is in `classes`; expression: raster calculator expression

minimum.description: range: lower bound, inclusive (in band units)

maximum.description: range: upper bound, inclusive (in band units)

derivative.description: range only: quantity the bounds apply to. With anything but `value` the band is read as a DTM (elevation model) and the bounds are in degrees / percent / etc.

segments.description: objects drawn on the raster (the SAM targets of the dock): WKT polygons in the CRS of the raster. When given, they are the selection: leave the range, classes and expression unset.

dock_objects.description: true: the objects the user drew on this raster in the FilterMate dock are the selection (map_context lists them as drawn_objects). Leave everything else unset, segments included.

raster_selection.description: REQUIRED when the source is a raster: which pixels are the source area

anyOf.description: Points kept on a point cloud (ASPRS classes, ranges, return number, expression).

classes.description: ASPRS classification codes kept (0-255), e.g. 2 ground, 3-5 vegetation, 6 building, 9 water

z_min.description: Minimum Z (elevation), in the layer CRS units

z_max.description: Maximum Z (elevation), in the layer CRS units

expression.description: Point cloud expression (e.g. Classification = 6 AND Z > 1000), ANDed with the other criteria

point_cloud_criteria.description: Point cloud source: which points make the source area (omit = the points it shows now)

filter_source.description: Raster source: also mask the source raster outside the selection

tools.name: geometry_filter
tools.title: Filter by a WKT geometry
tools.description: Filter layers of any kind by a WKT geometry (a drawn area, an extent, a commune outline). Same effect and answer as cross_filter, with a geometry given inline instead of a source layer: the way to filter by an area when no source feature can be selected in QGIS. Replaces the previous filter of each target unless operator is given. Not in the undo history: revert with clear_filters. Returns filtered, failed, skipped and warnings.

crs.description: CRS of the geometry, authority code such as EPSG:2154 or EPSG:4326 (the coordinate order is x/longitude first)

target_layers.description: Layers to filter, of any kind: layer ids or names

predicates.description: Spatial predicates, each tested as `target <predicate> source`: Intersect (share any space), Contain (the target contains the source), Disjoint (share nothing; rasters and point clouds then keep the outside of the source), Equal (same geometry), Touch (borders meet, interiors do not), Overlap (partial overlap of same-dimension geometries), Are within (the target lies inside the source), Cross (lines crossing). A target is kept when ANY listed predicate holds.

buffer.description: Buffer applied to the geometry, in the units of the CRS of the first target

coverage_min.description: Polygon targets only: minimum share (%) of the target inside the geometry

operator.description: How to combine with the previous filter of each target: AND (keep what both filters keep), OR (keep what either keeps), AND NOT (remove the new selection from the previous filter, or from the whole layer when it has none). Omit to replace the previous filter.

tools.name: point_cloud_filter
tools.title: Filter point clouds
tools.description: Keep only some points (by class, elevation, intensity, return number or expression) on point cloud layers. The same criteria apply to every listed layer, e.g. all the tiles of a LiDAR HD dataset. Sets the layer filter (e.g. 'Classification = 6 AND Z >= 1000'). It is one step of the dock's history of those point clouds (the dock's Undo on the layer reverts it) but undo_filter does not undo it: revert with clear_filters. Returns done (layers filtered), failed and skipped.

layers.description: Point cloud layers (LiDAR tiles...): layer ids or names

criteria.description: Points to keep; at least one criterion is required

classes.description: ASPRS classification codes kept (0-255), e.g. 2 ground, 3-5 vegetation, 6 building, 9 water

z_min.description: Minimum Z (elevation), in the layer CRS units

z_max.description: Maximum Z (elevation), in the layer CRS units

expression.description: Point cloud expression (e.g. Classification = 6 AND Z > 1000), ANDed with the other criteria

operator.description: How to combine with the previous filter of each target: AND (keep what both filters keep), OR (keep what either keeps), AND NOT (remove the new selection from the previous filter, or from the whole layer when it has none). Omit to replace the previous filter.

tools.name: clear_filters
tools.title: Clear filters
tools.description: Put layers back on their original source with no filter (the dock's Unfilter). Removes subset strings and restores the original source of raster and point cloud layers that were clipped. This is the way to revert cross_filter, geometry_filter, point_cloud_filter and apply_favorite. Returns done, failed and skipped.

layers.description: Layers of any kind to unfilter: layer ids or names

tools.name: apply_favorite
tools.title: Apply a favorite
tools.description: Apply a saved favorite, as the dock's favorites menu does. Returns the step (layer_name, expression, is_clear) and active_filters. The favorite id must exist: use list_favorites first.

tools.name: zoom_to
tools.title: Zoom the map
tools.description: Zoom the QGIS map to a layer, to its selected features, to a WKT extent, or to everything (no argument). Changes only the view, never the data or the filters. Returns extent_wkt and scale after the zoom. Fails without a map window (headless QGIS).

layer.description: Layer id or name to zoom to (its whole extent, or its selection with selected_only)

extent_wkt.description: Instead of a layer: an extent or geometry as WKT

crs.description: CRS of the WKT, e.g. EPSG:2154

selected_only.description: With layer: zoom to its selected features

tools.name: select_features
tools.title: Select features
tools.description: Select the features of a vector layer matching a QGIS expression, as the user would in QGIS. A selection is not a filter: the features stay visible, they are highlighted. Use it to make the source of cross_filter (which uses the selected features), or when the user asks to select. Returns layer_name and selected_count. Comparisons, IN, LIKE and simple text, number, date and geometry functions are accepted; other functions are refused.

expression.description: QGIS expression (NOT SQL), plain conditions only: "population" > 10000, "nom" ILIKE 'saint%', area($geometry) > 1000. Field names in double quotes, text in single quotes.

clear.description: Empty the selection instead of selecting

add.description: Add to the current selection instead of replacing it

tools.name: set_layer_style
tools.title: Style a layer
tools.description: Change how a layer is drawn on the map: one symbol, categories, graduated classes, a raster ramp. Returns mode, field, classes (how many were made), ramp, method, and for a raster band, minimum and maximum. The values of the classes are not returned: describe_layer and layer_statistics read the data. A field with more than 100 values cannot be categorized. In the chat of FilterMate, undoing the turn brings the previous style back.

mode.description: Vector: single (one symbol, color), categorized (one color per value of field), graduated (classes of a numeric field). Raster: pseudocolor (a color ramp over band values), gray (a gray stretch)

ramp.description: Color ramp of QGIS: Viridis, Spectral, Blues, Reds, Greens, RdYlGn, Magma, Turbo...

method.description: graduated: how the class breaks are found

minimum.description: Raster: lowest value of the ramp (statistics by default)

maximum.description: Raster: highest value of the ramp

tools.name: set_labels
tools.title: Label a layer
tools.description: Write the values of a field next to the features of a vector layer on the map, or turn the labels off. Returns labels (on or off) and field. In the chat of FilterMate, undoing the turn brings the previous labels back.

field.description: Field whose values are written on the map

buffer.description: A light halo around the text, to read it on any background

tools.name: update_features
tools.title: Edit attributes of features
tools.description: Change attribute values of features, in the edit buffer of the layer: nothing is saved. The layer goes into editing mode; the user reviews the changes and saves them (Save Layer Edits) or discards them. Choose the features with expression and/or selected_only. Keys, joined and virtual fields are not changed; a value that does not fit its field is refused. Returns changed (features), editing and unsaved. In the chat of FilterMate, undoing the turn takes the changes back while they are not saved.

values.description: Field: value, each converted to the type of its field (a number, a text, true or false, null)

formulas.description: Field: QGIS expression computed on each feature, such as "pop" * 2 or round($area / 10000, 2)

expression.description: QGIS expression choosing the features ("nom" = 'Muret'); the expression true for every feature

tools.name: delete_features
tools.title: Delete features
tools.description: Delete features of a vector layer, in its edit buffer: they are gone from the data once the user saves. Only when the user asks to delete features; to hide them, filter the layer instead. The chat of FilterMate asks the user first. Returns deleted, editing and unsaved.

tools.name: add_features
tools.title: Add features
tools.description: Add features to a vector layer from WKT geometries and attributes, in its edit buffer: nothing is saved. Returns added, editing and unsaved. In the chat of FilterMate, undoing the turn takes them back while they are not saved.

features.description: [{"wkt": "POINT(1.44 43.6)", "attributes": {"nom": "Puits"}}]: geometries of the type of the layer

crs.description: CRS of the WKT, such as EPSG:4326; the layer's by default

tools.name: create_layout
tools.title: Make a print layout
tools.description: Make a print layout of the map: the map, a title, a legend, a scale bar and a north arrow on a page. It is added to the project, where the user opens it in the layout designer to finish it. Returns name, items, extent_from (given, layer, view or layers) and the scale of its map. export_layout writes it to a file. In the chat of FilterMate, undoing the turn removes it.

name.description: Name of the layout, new in the project

layers.description: Layers of the map; by default those checked in the layer tree

extent.description: [xmin, ymin, xmax, ymax] in the project CRS; by default extent_layer, then the map view

extent_layer.description: Show the whole of this layer

legend.description: A legend of the layers shown

tools.name: export_layout
tools.title: Export a print layout
tools.description: Write a print layout of the project as a PDF or PNG file in a sub-folder of the export root. A file of the same name there is overwritten. The chat of FilterMate asks the user first. Returns path (relative to the sub-folder) and bytes.

name.description: A layout of the project (map_context lists them)

subfolder.description: Sub-folder of the export root (a/b allowed, no ..)

tools.name: set_project_crs
tools.title: Set the CRS of the project
tools.description: Set the CRS of the project, which the map follows: what the user calls changing the CRS of the view. Layers in other CRS are reprojected on the fly, their data does not change. Returns crs, description, units, geographic and previous. In the chat of FilterMate, undoing the turn brings the previous CRS back.

crs.description: EPSG:2154 (Lambert-93), EPSG:4326 (WGS 84), EPSG:3857 (Web Mercator), an EPSG code alone, or a layer of the project whose CRS is taken

tools.name: add_field
tools.title: Add a field
tools.description: Add a field to a vector layer, in its edit buffer: nothing is saved until the user saves the layer edits. With a formula the field is filled on every feature at once. Returns layer_name, field, type, computed (the features filled), and formula_error when the formula was refused (the field is then added, empty). In the chat of FilterMate, undoing the turn removes the field.

length.description: Length of a text field; 0 lets the source choose

formula.description: QGIS expression computing the value of each feature ("pop" / $area * 1000000, upper("nom")); empty leaves the field empty

tools.name: join_layers
tools.title: Join a layer
tools.description: Join two layers by a field: the fields of join_layer show beside each feature of layer whose target_field equals its join_field, as the Joins tab of the layer properties does. Nothing is written to either source. Returns layer_name, join_layer and fields_added (as they are named in layer). In the chat of FilterMate, undoing the turn removes the join.

layer.description: Layer that gets the fields (id or name)

join_layer.description: Layer whose fields are shown beside it, a table without geometry too (id or name)

fields.description: Fields of join_layer to show; all of them by default

prefix.description: Put before the names of the fields shown; the name of join_layer and _ by default

tools.name: group_layers
tools.title: Put layers in a group
tools.description: Organize the layer tree: put layers in a group, made where it is missing, first or last of it; or just above another layer, to draw them over it. Layers keep their data, style and visibility. Returns group, groups_made, moved and not_found. In the chat of FilterMate, undoing the turn puts each layer back and removes the groups it made.

layers.description: Layer ids or names, in the order they take in the group

group.description: Group path from the top of the layer tree, such as Base or Base/Roads (made where missing); empty: the top of the tree itself

at_top.description: Put them first in the group (true) or last (false)

above.description: A layer: put them just above it, in its group, so they are drawn over it; group and at_top are then not used

tools.name: rename_layer
tools.title: Rename a layer
tools.description: Give a layer of the project another name, as shown in the layer tree and the legend; its data and source do not change. With group, rename a group of the layer tree instead. Returns layer_id, name and previous.

group.description: true: layer is the path of a group of the layer tree (Base/Roads), and that group is renamed

tools.name: bookmark
tools.title: Spatial bookmarks
tools.description: Spatial bookmarks of the project: named places the user goes back to (Bookmarks panel of QGIS). Returns action, name, bookmarks (all names), replaced, and extent_wkt after a zoom. In the chat of FilterMate, undoing the turn brings the bookmarks back as they were.

action.description: list the bookmarks; add one (the visible map, or extent_wkt; replaces a bookmark of that name); zoom the map to one; remove one

name.description: Name of the bookmark, for every action but list

extent_wkt.description: For add: the area as WKT (its bounding box is kept); the visible map by default

crs.description: CRS of extent_wkt; the CRS of the map by default

tools.name: map_theme
tools.title: Map themes
tools.description: Map themes of the project: saved views of which layers are shown, with their styles, used by layouts and by the user to switch views. Returns action, name, themes (all of them), replaced and layers_shown. In the chat of FilterMate, undoing the turn brings the themes, the visibility and the styles back.

action.description: list the themes; save the layers shown now and their styles under a name (replaces a theme of that name); apply a theme to the map; remove a theme

name.description: Name of the theme, for every action but list

tools.name: set_layers_visibility
tools.title: Show or hide layers
tools.description: Check or uncheck layers in the layer tree (shown or hidden on the map). Returns done and failed.

visible.description: true shows the layers, false hides them

tools.name: segment_objects
tools.title: Draw objects with SAM
tools.description: Draw with SAM, on a raster, the object each feature of a guide layer points at; adds them as a layer. The new polygon layer is a temporary GeoPackage, in the CRS of the raster, one object per guide feature, with the attributes of the feature, sam_score (the confidence of SAM, 0 to 1) and, for a polygon guide, sam_iou (overlap of the footprint with the drawn object, 0 to 1: a low value flags a footprint to look at, such as a building that changed, it does not prove a change). Then select_features on that layer (e.g. "sam_iou" < 0.5) or cross_filter with it as the source. No other layer is changed. Returns layer (layer_id, name, feature_count...), guide_features, drawn, without_object (features with no object: off the raster, nothing found by SAM, or never tried when stopped_early), sam_score {median, minimum}, sam_iou {median, minimum, below_half}, seconds and stopped_early (true when the 20 s allowed ran out before every window was drawn: call again with fewer features). QGIS is held while SAM draws, about 2 s for each window of 1024 pixels; other changes are refused meanwhile. A guide whose features cannot be counted (a web service) needs a selection. SAM (the model and its runtime) is installed by the user from the FilterMate dock; without it the call fails and says so. Good on buildings and other well delimited objects; parcels and trees are not reliable.

raster.description: Raster to draw on, as it shows on the map (an orthophoto): layer id or name

guide_layer.description: Vector layer whose features point at the objects: points (each a click on an object) or polygons (each a footprint: its bounding box and a point inside it). Layer id or name.

selected_only.description: Use the selected features of the guide; with none selected, the features it shows

limit.description: The most guide features taken in one call; a guide that gives more is refused, select fewer

name.description: Name of the layer added (default: the name of the guide followed by (SAM))

tools.name: similar_objects
tools.title: Find objects like an example with SAM
tools.description: Find with SAM, on a raster, the objects that look like an example; adds them as a layer. SAM draws the examples (with use_dock_object, every object drawn on the raster in the dock), then looks, window by window over the area searched, for the places whose encoder features look like one of them, draws them, and keeps those of 0.5 to 2 times their area (and shape) that look like one of them. The new polygon layer is a temporary GeoPackage with appearance (0 to 1, how much an object looks like the nearest example) and area_m2. Measured on buildings of a 25 cm orthophoto: about half of what it finds is right and it finds about a fifth of what is there, so say so to the user and let them check the layer; it is no census. Give the extent of the place meant, not more: past 20 s it stops (stopped_early) and an area of more than 64 windows of 1024 pixels is refused. Returns layer (null when nothing was found: no layer added), objects, examined, windows, windows_planned, stopped_early, seconds, examples {count, sam_score {median, minimum}, area_m2 {minimum, maximum}} and appearance {median, minimum}. QGIS is held while it searches; other changes are refused meanwhile. SAM is installed by the user from the FilterMate dock.

raster.description: Raster to search, as it shows on the map (an orthophoto): layer id or name

example_layer.description: Vector layer whose ONE selected feature (a point on the object, or its footprint) is the example; select it with select_features first. Leave empty with use_dock_object.

use_dock_object.description: The examples are the objects the user drew on this raster in the FilterMate dock (map_context lists them as drawn_objects): an object counts when it looks like any of them

extent_wkt.description: Area searched as WKT, e.g. map_context's extent_wkt; empty: the visible map

extent_crs.description: CRS of extent_wkt, e.g. EPSG:2154 (empty: the raster's)

same_shape.description: Keep only the objects shaped like the example (compactness within 0.5 to 2 times)

name.description: Name of the layer added (default: the raster name followed by (similar objects))

tools.name: add_layer
tools.title: Add a layer
tools.description: Add a layer to the open project from a local file or a public https URL. Typical use after search_open_data: pick a geojson or gpkg resource url and add it, then filter it like any other layer. A remote file is read where it is when its server gives parts of it (GeoPackage, GeoTIFF, zip); any other is first copied to the QGIS profile (512 MB and 3 minutes at most). When it cannot be added the error says why: try another resource of the dataset, or a service layer. Returns the layer summary (layer_id, name, layer_kind, provider_type, crs_authid, feature_count). The chat of FilterMate asks the user first.

source.description: A local data file on the QGIS machine (gpkg, shp, geojson, json, kml, gml, fgb, csv, tif; a GeoPackage table with |layername=name), or a public https URL of such a file (a resource url from search_open_data). Nothing else: no http, no provider URI, no database connection.

name.description: Name of the layer in the project (default: the file name)

tools.name: add_service_layer
tools.title: Add a layer of a WFS service
tools.description: Add a layer of a WFS service, read from the service as the map moves and filtered on the server. Only a layer the service lists can be added. Returns the layer summary. The chat of FilterMate asks the user first.

platform.description: A WFS platform the user allowed, e.g. ign_wfs (IGN Géoplateforme)

typename.description: Layer id given by search_open_data on that platform, e.g. ADMINEXPRESS-COG-CARTO.LATEST:commune

name.description: Name of the layer in the project (default: its title)

tools.name: search_imagery
tools.title: Search satellite imagery
tools.description: Find satellite scenes over an area, newest first, with the GeoTIFF of each one. Returns datasets [{id, publisher (collection), description (date and cloud cover), resources: [{format, url}]}]; format visual is the natural colour image. Then add_layer with its url and kind raster.

bbox.description: [west, south, east, north] in degrees; omit for the current map extent

platform.description: STAC catalog the user allowed, e.g. earth_search

tools.name: remove_layers
tools.title: Remove layers
tools.description: Remove layers from the project. Their files are not deleted. The chat of FilterMate asks the user first, and undoing the turn there brings the layers back with their styles and filters, except a layer held in memory, whose features are lost. From another client it cannot be undone. Returns done and failed.

layers.description: Layer ids or names to remove from the project

tools.name: search_open_data
tools.title: Search open data
tools.description: Search datasets on an open data platform the user allowed, and get the URLs a layer can be made of. Returns datasets [{id, title, publisher, description, page, resources: [{title, format, url}]}], the resources kept to files add_layer can open (geojson, gpkg, zip, csv, tif...). Then add_layer with a resource url (geojson or gpkg first), or add_service_layer with the id on a WFS platform. The query is sent to the platform.

query.description: Words to search, in the language of the platform

platform.description: datagouv (data.gouv.fr, France), opendatasoft (the public Opendatasoft hub), ign_wfs (IGN Géoplateforme layers), or a portal the user allowed

tools.name: export_layers
tools.title: Export filtered layers
tools.description: Write layers, as filtered now, to files on the QGIS machine, below the server's export root. Writes files: a file with the same name already in the sub-folder is overwritten. The files stay on the machine running QGIS; the answer gives their paths there. Returns done (layers written), outputs ({layer name: file path}), failed and skipped.

layers.description: Layers of any kind to export as they are filtered now, one file per layer: ids or names

subfolder.description: Sub-folder of the export root configured on the QGIS machine (a or a/b, letters, digits, _ . - only, no .. and never an absolute path)

crs.description: Output CRS such as EPSG:2154 (omit = each layer's CRS)
